title: Graph & Node Concepts
description: Build game logic by connecting event, action, and data nodes in the graph editor. Learn how execution flow, typed data ports, and edge modifiers work.

blocks.content: Visual scripting in Lupis Engine lets you create gameplay logic by wiring nodes together on an interactive canvas. You create scripts in the **Scripts** panel of the bottom dock, attach them to entities with a [Script Controller](components/script_controller), and edit their node graphs in workspace tabs.

items.title: Node Roles
items.desc: Combine **Event**, **Action**, and **Pure** nodes to trigger and process game logic.

items.title: Typed Data Ports
items.desc: Pass numbers, strings, booleans, lists, and maps through color-coded pins.

items.title: Direct & Variable Inputs
items.desc: Type values directly, bind a variable, or connect another node's output pin.

items.title: Edge Modifiers
items.desc: Click any data wire to apply math, string, or boolean operations inline.

blocks.content: Every node in the [Overview & Architecture](node_library/overview) catalog belongs to one of three roles. A node's role determines whether it starts execution, performs an action in sequence, or calculates data on demand.

rows: Starts an execution chain when an engine lifecycle callback, input, or signal fires.
Updates entity state, plays audio, moves bodies, or routes flow when triggered.
Computes or reads a value on demand whenever a connected Action node runs.

blocks.content: Nodes receive inputs on their left side and send outputs from their right side. Port colors indicate the data type carried by each pin and wire.

rows: Directs chronological execution order from one node's **execOut** to the next node's **execIn**.
Carries integers and decimals such as speed, health, timers, or coordinates.
Carries text values, entity IDs, tags, or animation clip names.
Carries true or false conditions for branches and state flags.
Carries ordered arrays of items managed with [Variables & Collections](visual_scripting/variables_and_collections).
Carries key-value dictionaries for structured data.
Accepts or outputs any data type.

blocks.message: Selecting a node displays its **Header**, **Parameters**, and **Ports Configuration** sections in the [Property Inspector](interface/property_inspector). In **Parameters**, click the toggle button next to any unconnected input to switch between **Direct Input** and **Variable** binding.

blocks.content: When you open a script tab from the **Scripts** panel, the left sidebar switches to **Variables** and **Node Library**, the center displays the graph canvas, and the right panel inspects the selected node or wire.

items: In the bottom bar, click **Scripts**, click **+** to create a script, and double-click the script to open its graph tab.
In the left sidebar under **Node Library**, search for a node or click **Open Node Library** to browse all 11 categories.
Double-click a node or drag it onto the canvas to place it.
Drag from a right-side output pin (**execOut** or a data output) to a left-side input pin on another node to connect a wire.
Select a node to edit its unconnected input values in the **Parameters** section of the [Property Inspector](interface/property_inspector).

Click any data wire between two nodes to open the **Edge Modifier** section, where you can apply inline operations such as **Add (+)**, **Multiply (x)**, **Append (Suffix)**, or **Invert (NOT !)** without adding an extra node.

blocks.message: Dynamic nodes such as [Switch](node_library/flow_logic#node-logicSwitch), [Add](node_library/math_operations#node-mathAdd), and [Set Transform](node_library/game_entity#node-setTransform) let you add or remove ports in **Parameters** or **Ports Configuration** using **+ Add Case**, **+ Add Value**, or **+ Select property...**.

blocks.content: Build a movement graph that reads directional keys every frame, scales the input vector with edge modifiers, and moves the entity.

items: Open your script in the graph editor and add an [On Tick](node_library/game_lifecycle#node-eventTick) node from [Scene & Lifecycle](node_library/game_lifecycle).

Add a [Calculate Axis 2D](node_library/input_controls#node-calculateAxis2d) node from [Input & Controls](node_library/input_controls) and a [Move and Slide](node_library/game_physics#node-moveAndSlide) node from [Physics & Collision](node_library/game_physics).
Connect **execOut** on **On Tick** to **execIn** on **Calculate Axis 2D**, then connect **execOut** on **Calculate Axis 2D** to **execIn** on **Move and Slide**.
Drag data wires from **axisX** and **axisY** on **Calculate Axis 2D** to **velocityX** and **velocityY** on **Move and Slide**.
Click each green data wire, set **Operation** to **Multiply (x)** in **Edge Modifier**, and set **Operand Value** to **200**.

Attach the script to an entity via [Script Controller](components/script_controller#add-the-component) and click **Play** in the [Scene Viewport](interface/scene_viewport) to move with **W**, **A**, **S**, and **D**.

rows: You want to attach scripts to an entity and override local variables in the inspector.
You want to store local or global data, lists, and maps.
You want to inspect node code or create custom JavaScript nodes.
You want to browse all built-in nodes across the 11 categories.
You want keyboard and mouse shortcuts for panning, selecting, and editing nodes.
